note: The Step-to-Move specialization verdict record, machine-readable
(SPEC-draft-pipeline "The Step↔Move instantiation contract" is the prose
half; kogaki#747, owner rulings
2026-09-01). src/compose.mjs READS these lists rather than restating
them, and checks/check-brief-compose.sh reads them too — this file is
the single carrier, so amending the vocabulary is one edit and never a
three-copy divergence. Same arrangement as src/record-schema.json and
src/gate-schema.json, deliberately.
WHAT THE HARNESS DOES WITH THIS FILE, stated here because the
distinction is the whole design: it VALIDATES a record against these
lists and it NEVER COMPOSES one. No default verdict exists, no verdict
is inferred from a Step's fields, and a missing record is a refusal
rather than a blank to fill. The judgment is the composing sitting's;
the mechanism owns only the record's shape and the refusal.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here; fifteen copies of it had
already drifted into eight variants, which is what kogaki#982 collapsed.
THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:
The Step↔Move instantiation contract
SPEC-draft-pipeline

candidate_id.rationale: a record composed against one Candidate cannot certify another — without this key a sitting could judge the Candidate it liked and adopt the one it wanted

verdict.one_per_step_rationale: a missing verdict and an extra verdict are both refusals, because a per-Step obligation that tolerates a short list is skippable one Step at a time

why_three_and_not_two: `cannot-determine` is a first-class value and not an escape hatch: a
two-valued read forces an honest non-answer to render as one of the
two answers, and the value that absorbs it is the passing one.
The served position is the same finding one domain over — a
two-valued exists→accepted read where the ratified rule is
three-valued and the honest value was cannot-determine
It does not weaken the gate: `passing` holds one member, so a
`cannot-determine` refuses exactly as `contradicts` does. What it buys
is that the refusal says WHICH — an unjudgeable Move contract and a
contradicted one need different repairs, and a two-valued record

refusal.rationale: the record's `why` is the one sentence the composing sitting wrote about that Step, so the refusal hands it back rather than paraphrasing it

note: THE RECORD IS DISCLOSURE, AND IT IS NOT A WRITE UNLOCK (kogaki#1108,
owner decision 2026-09-12).
WHAT STOOD HERE. A `ratification` block declared the gate
`brief-specialization-ratification`: a passing record was rendered to the
owner and adoption refused until they ratified it. Its ground was sound as
far as it went -- every verdict in the record is the composing sitting's
own, so a record of shape-valid `consistent` verdicts with no judgment
behind it used to reach the write with nothing beside it.
WHY IT IS GONE ANYWAY. It was a human gate over a MODEL VERDICT, which is
the shape the 2026-09-04 control-input ruling removes. The gate existed
because a passing model verdict was otherwise the only unlock on the Brief
write -- so it was covering for the fact that the Model owned the whole
composition, schema included. kogaki#1108 removes that: the Brief runs on a
Harness-owned workflow table, the path-composition state renders
src/step-schema.json into the prompt, and the executor validates every
judgment record against the state's own refusals. With the Model's freedom
confined to the field values of schemas the Harness declares, asking the
owner to ratify one of those records is a third question buying nothing the
other two do not already buy.
WHAT IS UNCHANGED. The record is still REQUIRED and still validated: a
missing record is a refusal, and a `contradicts` or `cannot-determine`
verdict still refuses adoption in path order with the same message. What
no longer exists is the owner act between a passing record and the write.
WHAT REPLACES IT. One sentence in the closing summary, naming the record's
digest and its verdict tally -- disclosure, on every adoption, rather than a
question on every adoption. The digest survives for that sentence and for
nothing else; it is no longer a binding key, because there is no capture
left to bind.

summary.shape: one sentence naming the record's digest and the tally of verdicts by value

digest.over: the canonical JSON [version, candidate_id, [[step_id, move, verdict, why], ...]] with verdicts in the ADOPTED PATH's order
digest.rationale: path order rather than record order, so a record whose verdicts are merely reordered digests identically and a record whose judgment changed does not. It names the record in the disclosure sentence; since kogaki#1108 it binds no capture, because no capture is taken
